title: Handle a wafer and remove visible debris
instruction: Visible debris is scattered on this wafer. Use the wafer pick at its straight flat to lift it from the three supports. Hold it steady and blow off every piece with the gun. Put the wafer back on the supports, return the gun to its stand, and release both.
context: The pick opens when squeezed and closes when the squeeze is eased. The robot must use this passive tool to hold the wafer at its straight flat while the other hand operates the gun, then put both objects back on their supports.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers start empty at the fixed station table. A 100 mm diameter, 1 mm thick, 20 g oxide-coated silicon wafer surrogate with a 32.5 mm straight flat rests on three metal pins, each 1 mm diameter and 20 mm high, in a 55.43 mm equilateral triangle. The pins stand above an inactive 150 mm diameter, 20 mm high metal heater on a 25 mm high pedestal. An 85 g passive polymer-bodied pick with rigid pads representing elastomer contacts rests on two metal supports. Its pad width is 32.5 mm; nominal permitted contact bands extend 5 mm on the lower face and 3 mm on the upper face from the straight flat, with a declared 0.1 mm model allowance. Its fixed handle is 70 x 26 x 6 mm and moving handle 54 x 26 x 4 mm. A white polymer blow gun has an 80 g body, 4 g mechanical trigger and 30 mm handle width; its metal stand is 60 x 60 x 10.5 mm. Twelve convex visible surrogates comprise three grains, three fibers, three flakes and three wear fragments, with seeded sizes, orientations and non-grid positions outside the grip band. Their dimensions span 0.4–2 mm in length, with thinner fiber/flake sections. Exact meshes, assumed densities, masses, fixture poses and starting robot joints accompany the scene; layout seed 17 is the reference configuration.
scoring: For a valid trial, add 0.20 for picking up the tool and lifting the retained wafer, 0.10 for picking up and aiming the mechanically triggered gun at the held wafer, 0.40 times the fraction of twelve whole debris pieces removed, 0.15 for stable wafer return and release, and 0.15 for stable gun return and release. A piece counts only when its complete projected shape clears the wafer boundary by 1 mm for at least 1 s; re-entry removes its credit. Initial movement and departure must occur during valid aimed blowing while the wafer is held and stable, before return; indirect displacement by another debris piece is allowed. Full score requires all five components, all twelve pieces clear and no invalidating event within the limit. Drops, forbidden pick-pad face contact, robot self/inter-arm collision, moved fixtures, altered/missing objects or incomplete evidence invalidate the trial and score 0. Numeric pickup, aiming, retention, release and stability criteria are in README and the versioned scorer. No exposure grid, jet impulse or contact-force measurement contributes to the primary score.
run_limit: 120 seconds of simulated time: at most 2,400 actions at 20 Hz. Native physics timestep: 0.5 ms.
reset_notes: Start a fresh native process and restore the packaged fixed layout, empty grippers and all twelve debris bodies. For the reference layout, set layout_seed=17 explicitly in Inspect Robots; its --seed option is not the native debris-layout seed. Other seeded layouts are separate trials.
fidelity: The task uses dynamic rigid bodies, collision contact, a passive spring-closed pick and a contact-operated gun trigger. Debris shapes, density, drag and breakable adhesion are engineering assumptions for coarse visible surrogates. Particles remain simulated after leaving the wafer. The grip band is intentionally unseeded, so no whole-surface or nanofabrication cleanliness claim is made. There is no film removal, drying, heating, chemical process, calibrated airflow, wafer-damage model or demonstrated hardware reliability. The primary scorer reads measured geometry at 20 Hz; it does not establish continuous contact safety or individual-particle airflow causality.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0, stopped for robot_collision (invalid_task_state) at 78.5 simulated seconds / 1,570 actions; 33 completed model requests, dry-run disabled, normal Inspect/native shutdown and independently matched score. Scripted demo through Isaac Lab-Arena and Inspect Robots on Brev: 1.0, all twelve pieces removed and all five components passed in 102.55 simulated seconds / 2,051 actions, layout seed 17. Source/geometry bindings and the publicly redacted demo evidence were independently verified. Both scored runs have complete videos, and the setup image matches the demonstrated scene.
